Topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections

Target audience: High school students or undergraduate geometry students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection

Lecture lines:
Imagine a double-napped cone sliced by a plane.
The cutting angle determines the shape of the slice.
We get circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

Planned animations:
Display a double-napped cone (#FFFFFF) and a intersecting plane (#FF9900).
Highlight the intersection path showing a circle (#00FF00).
Rotate the plane to show an ellipse (#00FF00).
Rotate the plane further to show a parabola (#00FF00).
Rotate the plane to show a hyperbola (#00FF00).

Section: section_2 — Introducing Dandelin Spheres

Lecture lines:
We place spheres inside the cone.
These spheres touch both the cone and plane.
Tangency points are the keys to conic geometry.

Planned animations:
Display a cone (#FFFFFF) and an inscribed sphere (#3399FF).
Bring a cutting plane (#FF9900) to touch the sphere.
Highlight the point of tangency between sphere and plane (#FF0000).

Section: section_3 — Geometric Proof: The Ellipse Case

Lecture lines:
Pick a point on our ellipse.
Distance to foci equals segment length.
Sums of these lengths stay constant.
This proves the classic ellipse definition.
The geometry is beautiful and simple.

Planned animations:
Show an elliptical cross-section with two Dandelin spheres (#3399FF).
Trace the distance from a point on the ellipse to the spheres' tangency points (#FFFFFF).
Demonstrate constant sum of these distances (#FF9900).

Section: section_4 — Generalizing to Parabola and Hyperbola

Lecture lines:
Parabolas need just one single sphere.
Hyperbolas require spheres in both nappes.
The plane cuts through the entire cone.

Planned animations:
Show a single sphere for a parabolic intersection (#3399FF).
Show two spheres, one in each cone nappe, for a hyperbola (#3399FF).
Highlight the distinct tangency points for these geometries (#FF0000).

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Conic sections appear in nature everywhere.
From orbital paths to architectural acoustics.
Dandelin spheres reveal their hidden logic.

Planned animations:
Display a Whispering Gallery room layout (#FFFFFF).
Animate sound waves bouncing between two elliptical focal points (#FF9900).
Fade out to show orbital mechanics planetary paths (#3399FF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Introducing Dandelin Spheres", [

        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2, direction=DOWN).set_color(WHITE).set_opacity(0.3)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.4).set_color("#3399FF")

        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
        plane.rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        # Tangency point (approx)
        self.place_at_grid(tangency_dot, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(tangency_dot))
        self.wait(2)
